title: Creatine in NZ
meta_desc: Discover the benefits of creatine monohydrate for NZ gym-goers, including evidence, dosing, and where to buy it in New Zealand, with prices and NZ brands compared.
intro: As a gym-goer in New Zealand, you're likely looking for ways to improve your performance and reach your fitness goals. One popular supplement that can help is creatine monohydrate. But what does it do, and is it right for you? In this guide, we'll cover the evidence, dosing protocol, and where to buy creatine in NZ, including a comparison of local brands and prices. We'll also discuss who benefits most from taking creatine and provide actionable tips you can use this week.

sections.heading: What is Creatine Monohydrate?
sections.body: Creatine monohydrate is a naturally occurring substance found in muscle tissue. It helps supply energy to your muscles, particularly during high-intensity activities like weightlifting and sprinting. Studies have consistently shown that creatine supplementation can increase muscle strength, power, and endurance. For example, a study published in the Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research found that creatine supplementation increased muscle strength by an average of 8% over a 12-week period. In NZ, you can find creatine monohydrate at most health food stores and online retailers, including local supermarkets like Countdown and New World.

sections.heading: Dosing Protocol
sections.body: The recommended dosing protocol for creatine monohydrate is to take 3-5 grams per day, divided into 2-3 doses. It's best to take creatine with a meal or snack that contains carbohydrates, as this can help increase absorption. For example, you could take 1-2 grams of creatine with your breakfast, and another 1-2 grams with your post-workout meal. Additionally, it's a good idea to cycle creatine for 8-12 weeks, followed by a 4-6 week break to allow your body to recover and maintain sensitivity to the supplement.

sections.heading: NZ Brands vs Imported
sections.body: There are several NZ brands that offer high-quality creatine monohydrate supplements, including Balance and Horleys. These brands often offer competitive pricing and convenient packaging options. However, some gym-goers may prefer to import creatine from international brands like Optimum Nutrition or MusclePharm. When comparing prices, be sure to check the ingredient label and look for third-party testing and certification, such as Informed-Choice or NSF International.

sections.heading: Who Benefits Most
sections.body: Creatine monohydrate is particularly beneficial for individuals who engage in high-intensity activities, such as weightlifting, sprinting, and jumping. It can also be helpful for athletes who require quick bursts of energy, such as rugby or football players. Additionally, creatine may be beneficial for older adults who are looking to maintain muscle mass and strength as they age. If you're looking for other affordable NZ protein sources or supplements, consider checking out Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme, which offers discounts on gym memberships and supplements for eligible individuals.

sections.heading: Get Started with Creatine
sections.body: If you're interested in trying creatine monohydrate, be sure to talk to a healthcare professional or registered dietitian to discuss your individual needs and goals. You can also compare prices and brands on our website, or take our quiz to find the best supplement for you.
